entries.meaning: The auxiliary charge alternator voltage is low as measured from the W/L terminal.

Shutdown and electrical-trip alarms can be disabled by user configuration; the alarm text is then displayed but the engine continues to run. Check the configuration before relying on any controller shutdown.
The engine speed has exceeded the pre-set trip. During start-up the overspeed trip logic can be configured to allow an extra margin ('Overspeed Overshoot') to prevent nuisance tripping.
The speed signal from the magnetic pickup is not being received by the controller.

Speed detection is factory configured from the main alternator output frequency; a flywheel magnetic pickup can be added by configuration; with CAN configured, speed comes over CAN. Rising oil pressure can disconnect the starter but cannot detect under- or overspeed.

entries.parameter: Controller DC supply (troubleshooting: unit shuts down)
entries.meaning: If the unit shuts down, check the DC supply voltage is not above 35 V or below 9 V. This is the controller module's own supply check, not a battery charging limit.

Make sure the magnetic pickup screen connects to earth at one end only (earthed at both ends it acts as an aerial and picks up random voltages); check the pickup is the correct distance from the flywheel teeth.

gaps: The configuration listing in this copy (PDF p. 110) shows placeholders (0 rpm, 0 V, 0%) for over/under-speed, battery and charge-alternator settings: no factory defaults are published in it. Trip settings remain per controller configuration — NOT VERIFIED.
Not checked against the current DSE7310 MKII / DSE7320 MKII manual (057-253); these entries apply only to the DSE7200 / 7300 series named.
